newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends broadly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends broadly lower in thin trade.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures finished broadly lower in dull trading Friday, pressured by light commission house selling, dealers said.
Turnover was meager at an estimated 3,549 lots, traders said.
"It was very, very thin and featureless," said one trader. "A 10-lot order was big in this market today."

Benchmark September arabicas ended down 4.10 cents at 176.30 cents a lb after ranging from 182.00 to 175.50. Second-month December ended 3.05 cents lower at 157.25 cents, while the back months shed 0.95 to 3.45.
Dealers said some trade selling of the September/December also weighed on the market. The switch narrowed to 19.05 cents, down from 20.10 cents at the close Thursday.
Coffee futures rose at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, on light trade buying. September's finish on Thursday above 180.00 cents was viewed by some market participants as constructive.
But a lack of follow-through buying and September's failure to test chart resistance at 184.50 cents prompted the reversal, dealers said.
Technically, traders said September support was seen near 174.25 cents. They continued to peg resistance at 184.50 cents -- a double top on the charts -- followed by 192.00 to 193.00 cents.

Despite today's losses, September coffee gained 12.00 cents -- or about seven percent -- on the week amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract.
After Friday's close, however, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 2,183 60-kg bags as of July 24, to 92,828 bags. An additional 3,738 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
